dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: The proposition asserting the existence of a positive real constant c for which a uniform exponential upper-tail bound holds for every finite family of independent, measurable, almost-surely bounded real-valued random variables on a probability space.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The target is definitionally this entire proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: A theorem supplying the AtLeastTwo certificate for the natural number 1 + 1.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supports elaboration of the numeral 2 appearing as the real multiplicative prefactor in the bound.

dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical conjunction of two propositions.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It conjoins positivity of the existential constant c with the universal tail-bound assertion.

dependency_coverage.name: DivInvMonoid.toDiv
dependency_coverage.meaning: The division operation projected from a division-inverse monoid structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies real division in the exponent, namely division of c t^2 by the sum of squared interval widths.

dependency_coverage.name: Exists
dependency_coverage.meaning: Existential quantification over an element of an inferred type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It quantifies the universal positive real constant c.

dependency_coverage.name: Filter.Eventually
dependency_coverage.meaning: A predicate holds eventually with respect to a filter when its truth set belongs to that filter.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Applied to the almost-everywhere filter of μ, it states that each X_i lies in its prescribed closed interval μ-almost everywhere.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.sum
dependency_coverage.meaning: The finite sum of a function over a finite set in an additive commutative monoid.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms both the centered random sum over i and the sum of squared interval widths over i.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.univ
dependency_coverage.meaning: The finite set containing every element of a finite type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes both sums range over all indices i in the finite index type ι.

dependency_coverage.name: Fintype
dependency_coverage.meaning: A structure exhibiting a type as finite and providing its finite enumeration.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It restricts the indexed family to a finite index type and makes summation over all indices available.

dependency_coverage.name: GE.ge
dependency_coverage.meaning: The greater-than-or-equal relation, defined by reversing the arguments of less-than-or-equal.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines the upper-tail event in which the centered sum is at least t.

dependency_coverage.name: HDiv.hDiv
dependency_coverage.meaning: The heterogeneous division operation supplied by an HDiv instance.

dependency_coverage.name: HPow.hPow

dependency_coverage.meaning: The heterogeneous subtraction operation supplied by an HSub instance.

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt

binders: There exists a real number c.

Universally quantified thereafter are a type ι, a type Ω, a finite-type structure on ι, a measurable-space structure on Ω, a measure μ on Ω equipped with a probability-measure instance, a family X : ι → Ω → Real, endpoint functions m M : ι → Real, and a real threshold t.
hypotheses: For every i ∈ ι, the function X_i : Ω → Real is measurable.
The family (X_i)_{i∈ι} is mutually independent with respect to μ.
For every i ∈ ι, X_i(ω) belongs to the closed interval [m_i, M_i] for μ-almost every ω.
conclusions: The real-valued measure of the event {ω | Σ_{i∈ι}(X_i(ω) - ∫ X_i dμ) ≥ t} is at most 2 exp(-(c t^2)/(Σ_{i∈ι} ‖M_i - m_i‖^2)).
mathematical_definitions: For each i, the centering constant is the real-valued measure-theoretic integral ∫_Ω X_i(y) dμ(y).
The centered sum is S(ω) = Σ_{i∈ι}(X_i(ω) - ∫_Ω X_i(y) dμ(y)).
The upper-tail event is A_t = {ω ∈ Ω | S(ω) ≥ t}.
The denominator is V = Σ_{i∈ι} ‖M_i - m_i‖^2; because the norm is the real norm, each term equals |M_i - m_i|^2.
The notation μ.real(A_t) means ENNReal.toReal applied to the measure μ(A_t).
Membership X_i(ω) ∈ Set.Icc(m_i,M_i) means m_i ≤ X_i(ω) and X_i(ω) ≤ M_i.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is a universal positive real constant c such that, for every finite family of mutually independent measurable real-valued random variables on any probability space, if each X_i lies between m_i and M_i almost surely, then for every positive t the probability that the sum of the centered variables is at least t is no greater than 2 times the exponential of -c t squared divided by the sum of the squared interval widths.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The estimate is one-sided: the event uses the centered sum ≥ t, not an absolute value or a two-sided deviation event.
The index type may be any finite type, including the empty type.

The endpoint functions m and M are arbitrary; no explicit hypothesis m_i ≤ M_i is present. If a required interval is empty, the almost-everywhere bound is impossible under a probability measure, so the implication can hold vacuously.
The interval bounds hold only μ-almost everywhere, not at every point of Ω.
The threshold is restricted to strictly positive real t.
The conclusion asserts only the existence of some positive universal c and gives neither a numerical value nor an optimality claim.
Real division in Lean is total. If Σ_i ‖M_i - m_i‖^2 = 0, the quotient is interpreted using division by zero, hence as 0, so the right side becomes 2 and the estimate is correspondingly trivial.

The integral is used without a separately stated integrability hypothesis. Under consistent finite almost-sure bounds on a probability space, measurability yields the expected integrability, while inconsistent bound assumptions make the implication vacuous.
The conclusion uses μ.real, the toReal conversion of the extended-nonnegative measure. Finiteness is ensured by the probability-measure assumption.
No pointwise boundedness, identical distribution, common interval, nonempty index type, or positive denominator is required.
